subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored `/exec` session defaults continue to override later global `tools.exec` config for Discord sessions, or should operator config changes reset or outrank those stored session fields?
rationale: Current main treats `/exec` as persistent per-session state and docs say it updates session state; changing that alters a shipped security/session contract rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Make global config authoritative
options.body: Stored session exec fields would be cleared or ignored when operator config changes, prioritizing central security control over persistent session convenience.

options.title: Keep persistent session overrides
options.body: The current `/exec` contract remains, and docs/operator tooling should explain how to inspect and clear stale session exec defaults.

options.title: Add reset or doctor first
options.body: Keep runtime precedence for now but add an operator-visible session exec reset or doctor repair before changing default semantics.

recommendation.title: Make global config authoritative
recommendation.body: Stored session exec fields would be cleared or ignored when operator config changes, prioritizing central security control over persistent session convenience.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the `/exec` session override contract and later clarified exec docs/defaults, making him the strongest available owner for the policy choice.
